question: to the Commission Barry Cowen (Renew) Subject:

The Vision for Agriculture and Food and the Safe Hearts Plan, presented by the Commission in 2025, highlight the importance of promoting the reformulation of food and drink products, while ensuring a high level of consumer protection and public health. However, the food and feed safety omnibus of 16 December 2025 does not include specific measures to support further innovation in this area. The ‘30 % energy-reduction rule’ in the Food Additives Regulation (Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008) allows the use of low- or no-calorie sweeteners only where the final product has at least 30 % lower energy content than a comparable product. Stakeholders have raised concerns that this threshold may limit manufacturers’ ability to pursue incremental sugar-reduction strategies, particularly where significant reductions have already been achieved. 1.

How does the Commission assess whether the 30 % energy-reduction threshold remains appropriate in light of its objectives to support public health through sugar reduction, while also promoting innovation and competitiveness?
Does the Commission intend to review Article 7(a) of the Food Additives Regulation to assess whether the threshold remains proportionate and fit for purpose?
What scientific and policy rationale underpins the threshold and has the Commission assessed its impact on incremental reformulation efforts and product innovation?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.9.2026) A food additive may be included in the Union lists of Authorised additives1 only if it does not pose a safety concern to the health of the consumer, there is a reasonable technological need that cannot be achieved by other economically and technologically practicable means, its use does not mislead the consumer and it has advantages and benefits for the consumer. For food additives belonging to the functional class of sweeteners, additional specific conditions2 must be met. Among those additional conditions, the ‘30 % energy-reduction threshold’3 referred to by the Honourable Member was included in the Food Additives Regulation4 to ensure a significant energy-reduction and thus clear benefits from replacing sugars by sweeteners in foods. This guarantees a meaningful reformulation that provides a legitimate nutritional advantage by comparison with foods containing sugars. The restriction also ensures that the use of sweetener food additives is limited to certain products within specific food categories, as set out in Annex II of the Food Additives Regulation. The Commission considers that the rationale underpinning this restriction remains relevant and does not intend to review Article 7(a) of the Food Additives Regulation. In the broader context of improving dietary habits, the Commission supports efforts to reduce sugar consumption, including through the food industry-led EU Code of Conduct on Responsible Food Business and Marketing Practices and through Food 20305, as well as support to national reformulation initiatives6 The Annex on Added Sugars of the 2015 EU Framework for National Initiatives for Selected Nutrients7 indicates as preferred outcome that the reduction of added sugars also leads to a reduction of the sweet taste.
1 In Annexes II and III to Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16

December 2008 on food additives (OJ L 354, 31.12.2008, p. 16). 2 A food additive may be included in the Union list in Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 for the functional class of sweetener only if it serves one or more of the following purposes: (a) replacing sugars for the production of energy-reduced food, non-cariogenic food or food with no added sugars; or (b) replacing sugars where this permits an increase in the shelf-life of the food; or (c) producing food intended for particular nutritional uses as defined in Article 1(2)(a) of Directive 89/398/EEC. 3 Article 3(2) f of Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 defines ‘energy-reduced food’ as a food with an energy value reduced by at least 30 % compared with the original food or a similar product. 4 Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on food additives OJ L 354, 31.12.2008, pp. 16–33. 5 the research and innovation policy framework deployed under the Horizon Europe programme. 6 European Commission, Communication on an EU cardiovascular health plan: the Safe Hearts Plan, COM(2025) 1024 final, 16 December 2025. 7 Available at https://health.ec.europa.eu/publications/added-sugars-annex-eu-framework-national-initiativesselected-nutrients_en.
